Hi Tessa —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We reviewed the draft MSA/order form and the DPA your team sent. I attached a version of the DPA with our preferred redlines (Biomed_DPA_redline_v2.docx). High level items we need clarified before legal will advance:

- SCCs: we prefer the 2021 SCCs with controller-to-processor Annexes. Can Redwood confirm which SCC module you intend to use and whether you will sign as processor?
- Subprocessor disclosures: need a commitment to notify 30 days prior to adding any EU-based subprocessor that handles PHI/PII.
- Transfer Impact Assessment (TIA): can you share any recent TIAs for the EU->US flows and the mitigations used (encryption in transit, contractual protections)?
- Roles: we have a question about whether certain analytics outputs are treated as derived data and whether Redwood requests any rights beyond processing.

We have a tight procurement window (contract needs to be signed by Oct 20). Please escalate if needed — our compliance lead is on this thread.

Thanks,
Elena

Two quick clarifications from compliance:

- Regarding SCCs: our procurement prefers Processor Annex (module) with explicit subprocessors listed in an exhibit. If Redwood signs as processor, we need a mechanism to publish an EU-only processor list.

Date: Fri, 9 Oct 2026 10:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form + DPA questions

Elena / Biomed team —

Thanks for the redline and the context. I did a legal pass and summarized the position below. I’ve attached a short Order Form redline that aligns with the DPA positions we’re comfortable taking (OrderForm_v3-redline.pdf).

Summary of Redwood position and open items:
- SCCs: Redwood will execute the 2021 SCCs, module(s) to be agreed (we typically sign as Processor for standard SaaS data flows). We will include a Processor Annex where applicable.
- Subprocessors: Redwood can accept 30 days’ notice for new subprocessors, but cannot agree to an opt-out that vetoes all changes — we propose a right for Biomed to object in writing and de-escalate to a remediation plan during the notice period.
- TIA: We can provide a redacted high-level TIA summary (controls, encryption, endpoint protections) and a dated statement of assessments. Full TIA with sensitive configs is available under NDA/secure share — David, please see action below.
- Derived outputs / IP: Redwood does not claim ownership of customer data or customer-derived outputs. We request a narrow processing license to operate (ingest/process/return) and to improve service quality in aggregate non-identifiable form — we are willing to carve out any clause that suggests ownership of Biomed-specific derived IP.
- Export controls & local law exceptions: Redwood will accept exceptions limited to documented legal compulsion and will add a notice/consultation requirement prior to any compelled disclosure.

Open items remaining:
1) Order Form wording for EU-residency (if Biomed requires dedicated EU-only deployment there will be pricing/ops implications). Aditya — can you confirm whether EU residency is feasible for this deal and what the delta would be?
2) TIA delivery path: David to prepare a redacted TIA summary and confirm whether additional NDA is required to share the full report.

Proposed near-term plan:
- Triage call Thurs 9 Oct 17:00 UTC / Fri 10 Oct 10:00 CET (please confirm).
- Laura to provide annotated DPA positions by end of day Mon 12 Oct.
- Once final redlines agreed, route MSA + Order Form + DPA to DocuSign (target signature window Oct 13–16).

Attachments: OrderForm_v3-redline.pdf

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
